 Invesco QQQ Trust ( QQQ ) was the sole fund in this report, and its ETF activity on Monday was entirely one-sided: QQQ bought $2.44 billion of stock and sold nothing, increasing all 101 of its positions and decreasing none. The fund's assets under management stand at $463.70 billion.

 Its largest buys by dollar value were AAPL ($206.7 million), NVDA ($173.9 million) and MSFT ($163.5 million).

 The largest buy was Apple Inc, where QQQ added 589,392 shares worth $206.7 million, lifting the position to 8.47% of assets. NVIDIA Corp followed with 973,224 shares added for $173.9 million at a 7.13% weight, then Microsoft Corp with 299,880 shares for $163.5 million at 6.7%. Amazon.com Inc drew $116.3 million on 435,528 shares at 4.76%, and Advanced Micro Devices Inc added 182,016 shares worth $92.6 million at 3.79%. None of the buys were new positions and there were no exits, as the fund reported no sells. 
 How does QQQ invest? 
 QQQ is an equity fund holding 101 stocks, with 46.7% of assets in its 10 largest holdings. Technology accounts for 55.6% of the stocks that could be classified, Communication Services 11.9% and Consumer Cyclical 11.7%, and the portfolio is 100.0% large-cap. Its expense ratio is 0.18%, and its top holdings are Apple Inc at 8.47%, NVIDIA Corp at 7.13%, Microsoft Corp at 6.7%, Amazon.com Inc at 4.76% and Advanced Micro Devices Inc at 3.79%. The fund has a GF Score of 89, a P/E of 22.8, a P/B of 7.02, a dividend yield of 0.45% and a year-to-date return of 10.21%.

 Story Continues What should investors watch next for QQQ?
